title: Twenty-minute ops simulator: seller playlet & rapid runbook (draft)
content:
Context / why this exists:
- Field feedback: sellers and SEs need a compact, reproducible rehearsal for incident-style objections (latency spikes, quota exhaustion, private deploy constraints).
- Goal: give a 20-minute guided run for a seller + SE to roleplay an escalation, validate talking points, and practice invoking fallbacks (model variant, routing policy, reserved capacity).
- Format: micro-deck (6 slides) + 3 scenario playlets + a 20-minute timed script for the seller and SE.

Target audience:
- Primary: Sales Engineers / Platform Sellers prepping for a pilot or executive briefing.
- Secondary: Account Execs, Customer Success leads who join technical calls.

Topline message (one-liner):
"Get customers back to serving value in under 20 minutes: proven runbook for diagnosing inference regressions, switching to safe fallbacks, and preserving production SLAs."

Deck outline (6 slides) — rough, annotated for speaker notes:
1) Title + framing (30s)
   - Slide items: title, TL;DR (what this runbook accomplishes), timebox.
   - Speaker note: "We’ll run a live roleplay: diagnose -> iterate -> recover. Observability and quick levers are what keep things online."
2) Runbook at a glance (90s)
   - Flow: detect -> triage -> remediate -> validate -> close
   - Quick hooks: tracer IDs, cost delta, token-per-request spike, model fallback mapping.
3) Three scenariotypes (180s)
   - Scenario A: sudden latency spike on hosted API during a demo (cause: noisy long-context requests)
   - Scenario B: pilot in Dedicated shows throughput collapse (cause: autoscale hit + KV cache inefficiency)
   - Scenario C: Private deployment regression after quantized model upgrade (cause: incompat kernel/precision)
   - For each: expected evidence, fastest mitigations, one-liners to reassure execs.
4) Playlet: 20-minute timed script (main slide)
   - Roles: Seller (S), Sales Engineer (SE), Customer (C)
   - Outcome goals: restore <2x baseline latency, preserve request fidelity, and commit next steps.
5) Fallback matrix (60s)
   - Quick rows: latency, quality, cost, security
   - Columns: hosted -> dedicated -> private; include example lines: "Switch to Llama-2-13b-v1-eco (quantized) for 10% lower token cost; route session via low-latency region"
6) After-action + follow-up (30s)
   - Evidence to collect, who owns action items, escalation timeline, patching note for product/infra.

20-minute timed run (script with cues) — use in rehearsal
- 00:00–01:00 Intro + set expectations (Seller): explain timebox and outcome.
- 01:00–03:00 Customer describes symptom. SE asks: "When did you first see this? any changes to prompt or traffic?"
- 03:00–06:00 Quick evidence triage (SE): check latency histograms, tail P95/P99, token-per-request distribution, error rate. If logs not available, ask for a recent sample request.
- 06:00–09:00 Hypothesis & hypothesis test (SE): propose 2 quick mitigations: 1) route to dedicated pool; 2) shorten max_tokens or reduce model size. Seller articulates business impact.
- 09:00–12:00 Apply first mitigation (Ops/Engineer simulated): toggle route or apply policy. Observe telemetry. If latency improves by >=30%, proceed to validation. If no improvement, fall back to plan B.
- 12:00–15:00 Customer-facing reassurance script (Seller): use 3 lines: acknowledge, explain action, next visible metric. Example lines: "We're rolling a targeted routing update now — you'll see latency drop on the next 10 requests. We’ll keep this session pinned until we confirm."
- 15:00–18:00 Validate: confirm tail latency, perform sample end-to-end check for quality regression. SE runs a quick deterministic prompt against both original and fallback model and reports differences.
- 18:00–20:00 Close: commit next steps (postmortem owner, follow-up demo scheduler), capture artifacts (trace ID, sample request, config change).

Three scenario playlets (short):
- Scenario A (demo spike)
  - Trigger: single heavy streaming request blocks worker pools.
  - Fast mitigations: shorten stream chunk size, enable request preempt on demo route, temporarily limit concurrency for demo user.
  - CEO-level script: "This is isolated to the demo route; we’ve throttled the intensive stream and latency will normalize immediately."

- Scenario B (Dedicated throughput collapse)
  - Trigger: autoscale hit due to sudden batch size change + large sequence length.
  - Fast mitigations: increase burst capacity (if reserved capacity allows), enable microbatching, or failover to compatible model variant.
  - SE checklist: check QPS, GPU utilization, pending queue length, model KV cache hit rate.

- Scenario C (Private regression after quantization change)
  - Trigger: model chokes on certain attention kernels, leads to quality drift.
  - Fast mitigations: rollback quantized artifact, enable software fallback to FP16 kernel in private infra, open internal incident to patch kernel selector.
  - Customer reassurance: "We’ve frozen the model version and will test the quantization in a staging region."

Key one-liners & objection responses (quick reference):
- "Why not just change the model?" -> "We prefer non-disruptive fallbacks first; change model only after we measure quality delta against your eval set."
- "Will this cost us more?" -> "Short-term routing to higher-tier may increase token-cost by X%; we’ll calculate and propose the minimal commit to restore SLA."
- "Is the private deployment safe to roll back?" -> "Yes — we keep pinned versions and an audited rollout, and we’ll coordinate a maintenance window if needed."

Metrics to capture during rehearsal (minimum):
- P50/P95/P99 latencies before and after
- Error rate and HTTP 5xx/4xx breakdown
- Token-per-request distribution and average tokens per minute
- Model output diff summary (BLEU-like or embedding distance snapshot)

Open questions / items to resolve (notes to self):
- Need a small script that auto-collects the three telemetry screenshots we ask for (P95 chart, queue length table, sample request). (ACTION: Ethan)
- Confirm preferred fallback model names and exact routing commands (console CLI snippets) to put on a cheat slide. (ACTION: Jonas)
- Legal needs a line explaining data retention when switching routes; ask CS for quick-approved phrasing. (ACTION: Samantha)

UX / slide polish notes (future):
- Slide 4 should have a 3-column live-updatable widget: "Status / Action / Expected delta" (mock as table until we can embed live cells).
- Add a 60s recorded demo (seller + SE) that teams can watch before prepping.

Next steps (for this draft):
- Get SE feedback via 11/30 dry run.
- Incorporate console CLI snippets + exact model variant tags.
- Convert to Google Slides once script and assets are stable.

Quick TODOs (short):
- [ ] Ethan: telemetry snapshot script prototype (due 2025-11-25)
- [ ] Jonas: canonical fallback mapping doc (due 2025-11-28)
- [ ] Samantha: legal blurb check-in (due 2025-11-29)
- [ ] Maya: schedule dry run with 2 SEs and 1 rep (target 2025-11-30)

Notes: this is intentionally compact — aim for reproducibility in a single call. Keep language customer-facing and low-technical when Seller leads; let SEs handle the diagnostic phrases.

References / related artifacts:
- Runbook draft on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTMP/Twenty-minute+Ops+Simulator
- Jira ticket for playlet tracking: JIRA:GTMP-842
- Draft seller scripts PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/seller-scripts/pull/128

End of draft.

(Notes to self: keep this doc short, produce a 6-slide starter, and make a 3-minute practice video. This file is intentionally workshop-y — will iterate after the dry run.)
